stand: Yemen's Saudi-backed government presses Operation Dawn of Yemen on three fronts: the Red Sea coast, Taiz and Marib. Forces claim Mocha and Dhubab near Bab al-Mandeb, though analysts say the Mocha claim was premature and Houthis deny losing either. Houthis have struck Aden's international airport, forcing a diverted flight, and claim fresh strikes on Riyadh, Abha and Khamis Mushait; a coalition, flying 100 jets, intercepted a missile north of Riyadh. Turkiye is sending technical and defensive support under the activated Mecca pact; Pakistan aids with reconnaissance.

claims.text: Yemen's government, backed by Saudi Arabia, launched Operation Dawn of Yemen to retake all Houthi-held territory, including Sanaa.
claims.by: Says: Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi, Presidential Leadership Council. Denies: —

claims.text: Houthi forces cut the main supply road linking besieged Taiz to the government's interim capital, Aden, encircling the city.
claims.by: Says: Yemeni security and military sources, via AFP. Denies: —

claims.text: Government forces say they recaptured the Red Sea port city of Mocha from the Houthis.
claims.by: Says: Yemeni government/Saba news agency. Denies: Houthi deputy governor of Taiz, Fuad Sinan.

claims.text: The Yemeni government's claim to have reached Mocha was premature, according to Yemeni military officials on the ground and analysts; fighting is concentrated around Dhubab district.
claims.by: Says: Yemen's government. Denies/disputes: Yemeni military officials on the ground and analysts.

claims.text: Saudi-led coalition says it has secured "air protection" over Bab al-Mandeb and destroyed hundreds of Houthi targets.
claims.by: Says: coalition spokesperson Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki. Denies: —; Al Jazeera says it could not independently verify.

claims.text: Houthis say they struck Saudi Aramco oil sites in Riyadh and Khurais with missiles and drones, causing large fires.
claims.by: Says: Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree. Denies: no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia.

claims.text: Three people were wounded in attacks on Jazan and Najran airports near the Yemen border.
claims.by: Says: Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation. Denies: —

claims.text: The latest fighting in Yemen has killed 959 people and wounded 4,207, Yemen's Ministry of Health and Population says.
claims.by: Says: Yemen's Ministry of Health and Population, via WHO. Denies: —

claims.text: More than 201,000 (201,217) people have been displaced since the war resumed, nearly all since 1 September, with Ta'iz governorate hardest hit.
claims.by: Says: International Organization for Migration, Director General Amy Pope. Denies: —

claims.text: Turkiye's support to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca pact is mainly defensive and technical — military equipment, intelligence sharing and weapons systems — not combat deployment.
claims.by: Says: Turkish and Saudi officials, via Reuters. Denies: —

claims.text: Yemen's Defence Ministry says Mocha has fallen; Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree now says Houthi fighters retain full control of all their advances.
claims.by: Says: Yemen's Defence Ministry. Denies: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree.

claims.text: 516,157 of Yemen's acutely malnourished children under five have the severe form of the condition, almost a quarter of the total.
claims.by: Says: United Nations, via Al Jazeera.

claims.text: Government-aligned Homeland Shield Forces launched a large-scale operation to retake Houthi-held al-Waziiya, west of Taiz; Houthis say they repelled the advance.
claims.by: Says: Yemen's army media centre, citing a military source. Denies: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree.

claims.text: A Saudi airstrike killed six members of one family, including four children, in Hajjah governorate.
claims.by: Says: Houthi health ministry.

claims.text: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched towards Khamis Mushait.
claims.by: Says: coalition spokesperson Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki.

claims.text: The coalition destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform in Sanaa and a Saada storage facility holding 20 ballistic missiles.
claims.by: Says: Saudi-led coalition, via Saudi Press Agency.

claims.text: Pakistani forces in Saudi Arabia are already playing a supporting, reconnaissance role; Saudi forces are conducting the actual combat.
claims.by: Says: Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif.

claims.text: Houthis attacked Aden International Airport with ballistic missiles and drones, forcing a flight from Cairo to divert to Jeddah.
claims.by: Says: Yemen's Ministry of Transport. Denies: —

claims.text: Houthis say they fired at a Saudi military supply convoy at Camp Badr near Aden airport; the government says its runway and passenger terminal were hit.
claims.by: Says: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree. Denies: Yemen's Transport Ministry, which says the runway and terminal were targeted.

claims.text: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched north of Riyadh.
claims.by: Says: Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki. Denies: —

claims.text: Houthis claim fresh strikes on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Abha airport and the Khamis Mushait air base.
claims.by: Says: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree. Denies: no immediate Saudi confirmation.

claims.text: WHO's immediate funding requirement for Yemen's health response has risen from $9 million to $31 million.
claims.by: Says: WHO Representative in Yemen, Dr Syed Jaffar Hussain. Denies: —

claims.text: Cholera cases in Yemen have tripled in three weeks, with cases detected in displacement camps.
claims.by: Says: World Health Organization. Denies: —

timeline.text: President Rashad al-Alimi announces in a televised address the start of Operation Dawn of Yemen to retake all Houthi-held territory.
Houthi fighters cut the main road linking Taiz to Aden, taking the al-Safiya area and its police station, encircling Taiz.
Houthis fire missiles and drones at Aramco sites in Riyadh and Khurais, claiming large fires; Saudi Arabia does not immediately confirm.
Government forces say they retook Dhubab district, its airport and the port city of Mocha; Houthis deny Mocha fell.
Saudi-led coalition launches an air campaign with 100 fighter jets, saying it has secured air protection over Bab al-Mandeb.
Government forces announce a strategic offensive on the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa.
Houthi fighters capture the town of Turbah in southwestern Yemen, advancing toward Taiz.
Saudi civil aviation authority says three people were wounded in attacks on Jazan and Najran airports near the Yemen border.
Defence ministers of Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia meet in Riyadh and agree to activate deterrence measures under their mutual defence pact.
Pakistan's defence minister says Pakistani forces are already providing reconnaissance support in Saudi Arabia; combat remains Saudi-led.
Yemen's Defence Ministry says Mocha has fallen; a Houthi military spokesman denies any retreat, calling reports "fabricated heroics".
Government and allied Popular Resistance Forces say they took the al-Manzara, al-Ashari and Dhiban mountains in Haifan, south of Taiz.
WHO says the fighting has killed at least 959 people and wounded 4,200+; IOM says over 184,000 have been displaced since the war resumed.
Houthis claim fresh strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid airport, the Rabigh Aramco refinery, Abha airport and the Khamis Mushait base; Riyadh does not confirm.
Government-aligned Homeland Shield Forces launch a large-scale operation to retake Houthi-held al-Waziiya, west of Taiz; Houthis say they repelled it.
Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Khamis Mushait.
Coalition says it destroyed a missile launch platform in Sanaa and a Saada depot holding 20 ballistic missiles.
Houthi health ministry says a Saudi strike killed six members of a family, four of them children, in Hajjah.
AFP sources on both sides say fighting across Yemen killed more than 270 government troops and Houthi fighters in a single day.
WHO warns of a critical funding gap for Yemen's health response as needs rise and trauma points go unstaffed.
Houthis attack Aden International Airport with ballistic missiles and drones; a flight from Cairo is diverted to Jeddah and the terminal evacuated.
Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched north of Riyadh.
Houthis claim fresh strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid airport, Abha airport and the Khamis Mushait air base; Riyadh does not confirm.
IOM says Yemen displacement has passed 200,000, reaching 201,217, with Ta'iz governorate hardest hit.
Turkiye says its support to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca pact is mainly defensive and technical, not combat deployment.
Yemeni military officials and analysts say the government's claim of reaching Mocha was premature; fighting is concentrated in Dhubab district.
Houthis sweep down Yemen's Red Sea coast, seizing about 150km of coastline and areas around Bab al-Mandeb.
